finding: Missing <meta name="viewport"> tag — page will not scale correctly on mobile devices
recommendation: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> inside <head>

finding: Viewport meta disables user zoom (user-scalable=no) — violates WCAG 1.4.4 and hurts accessibility
recommendation: Remove user-scalable=no or user-scalable=0 from the viewport meta. Let users pinch-zoom.

finding: Viewport restricts zoom to 1x (maximum-scale=1) — blocks users who need to enlarge text
recommendation: Remove maximum-scale=1 or increase it to at least 5. This violates WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text.

finding: Page has horizontal scroll — content is wider than the mobile viewport
recommendation: Find elements with fixed pixel widths wider than the viewport. Use max-width: 100%, overflow: hidden on containers, or width: 100vw carefully (accounting for scrollbar).

finding: Touch target is smaller than 44×44px — hard to tap accurately on mobile
recommendation: Increase padding to make the tappable area at least 44×44px. Don't change visual size — use padding or ::after pseudo-elements to expand the hit area.

finding: Interactive elements are too close together — risk of mis-taps on mobile
recommendation: Ensure at least 8px gap between adjacent tap targets. Group related actions with clear visual separation.

finding: Body font size is below 16px — iOS will auto-zoom form inputs, disrupting the layout
recommendation: Set body font-size to at least 16px. This prevents iOS Safari from automatically zooming in when users tap on inputs.

finding: Paragraph/list text is below 14px — difficult to read on mobile without zooming
recommendation: Use at least 14px (ideally 16px) for body copy on mobile. Small text forces users to pinch-zoom, increasing reading friction.

finding: Email input does not use type="email" — mobile keyboard won't show @ symbol by default
recommendation: Add type="email" to email inputs. This triggers the mobile email keyboard (with @ and .com keys) and enables basic validation.

finding: Phone/tel input does not use type="tel" — mobile keyboard shows QWERTY instead of number pad
recommendation: Add type="tel" to telephone inputs. This shows the numeric dial pad keyboard on iOS and Android, making number entry much faster.

finding: Numeric input does not use type="number" or type="tel" — mobile shows QWERTY keyboard for number entry
recommendation: Use type="number" for numeric-only values, or type="tel" if you want the dial pad without the increment/decrement arrows.

finding: Form inputs lack autocomplete attributes — mobile users can't use saved data to fill forms faster
recommendation: Add autocomplete attributes: name, email, tel, address-line1, postal-code, etc. Dramatically reduces typing effort on mobile.

finding: Form field relies on placeholder text as label — placeholder disappears when user starts typing on mobile
recommendation: Add a visible <label> element to every input. Placeholder text should hint at format/example, not replace the label. When typing starts, the label is gone and users lose context.

finding: Form field is shorter than 44px — hard to tap on mobile and may trigger iOS auto-zoom
recommendation: Set min-height: 44px on all form fields. This satisfies touch target guidelines and prevents iOS zoom. A common pattern is padding: 12px 16px.

finding: Images or videos may overflow the mobile viewport — no max-width constraint detected
recommendation: Add img, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } globally. This single rule prevents most image overflow issues on mobile.

finding: No mobile navigation toggle detected — desktop navigation may be hidden with no mobile alternative
recommendation: Ensure a hamburger/menu button is present and functional on mobile. Verify the desktop nav collapses and a clear toggle appears.

finding: A fixed/sticky element covers more than 20% of the mobile viewport height — reduces usable screen space
recommendation: Fixed elements (headers, chat widgets, cookie banners) should be as compact as possible on mobile. A sticky header should collapse to ≤60px. Avoid fixed footers unless they're the primary CTA.

finding: Primary CTA button is not visible above the fold on mobile — users must scroll to take action
recommendation: Place the primary CTA within the first viewport on mobile. If content is long, use a sticky CTA bar at the bottom or a floating action button.

finding: No search functionality detected on mobile — users on small screens rely heavily on search to navigate
recommendation: Ensure search is prominently accessible on mobile. A search icon in the header (opens full-screen search) is the standard mobile pattern.

finding: Data table found — tables often cause horizontal scroll on mobile if not wrapped in a scrollable container
recommendation: Wrap tables in a div with overflow-x: auto. Consider converting tables to card-based layouts for complex data on mobile.

finding: Navigation links detected — verify they have enough vertical padding for mobile tapping (minimum 44px height)
recommendation: Set padding: 12px 16px on navigation links minimum. Stacked mobile nav items should have clear visual dividers and generous tap areas.

finding: Viewport meta does not set initial-scale=1 — page may render at wrong scale on some browsers
recommendation: Use <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> for consistent rendering across all mobile browsers.

finding: Scroll event listeners detected — if not marked passive, they can block scrolling and cause jank on mobile
recommendation: Add { passive: true } to all scroll/touch event listeners: element.addEventListener('scroll', fn, { passive: true }). This eliminates 60fps scroll jank on mobile.

finding: Default tap highlight color may create visual flash on tap — no -webkit-tap-highlight-color override found
recommendation: Add -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent to interactive elements if using custom tap feedback. Or ensure the default highlight matches your brand colors.

finding: Video/audio with autoplay lacks muted attribute — will be blocked by iOS/Android and may surprise users
recommendation: Always add muted to autoplaying videos. Mobile browsers block unmuted autoplay. The pattern video[autoplay][muted][playsinline] works cross-platform.

finding: Video element lacks playsinline attribute — will open fullscreen player on iOS instead of playing inline
recommendation: Add playsinline to all video elements. Without it, iOS forces videos into fullscreen mode, breaking the intended layout.
